BILL NUMBER:  S3812

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law and the public officers
law, in relation to owner liability for failure of operator to comply
with traffic control indications; and providing for the repeal of such
provisions upon expiration thereof


 PURPOSE :
This bill authorizes the city of Syracuse to adopt a local law that
would allow for the installation of traffic control photo violation
monitoring systems ("Red Light Cameras") at up to fifty intersections
throughout the city and provide for violations not to exceed fifty
dollars thereof.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Section 1. Amends subdivision 1 of section 235 of the VTL to make
technical changes.

Section 2. Amends section 235 of the VTL to make technical changes.

Section 3. Amends VTL section 235 to make technical changes.

Section 4. Amends subdivision 1 of section 236 of the VTL to make
technical changes.

Section 5. Amends subdivision 1 of section 236 of the VTL to authorize
the city of Yonkers to adopt a local law establishing a red light
camera demonstration program at twenty-five intersections throughout
the county and imposing monetary fines for violations thereof.  The
section further outlines the parameters for establishment of such a
program as well as penalty provisions.

Section 6. Amends subdivision 10 of section 237 of the VTL to make
technical changes.

Section 7. Amends section 237 of the VTL to make technical and
conforming changes.

Section 8. Amends paragraph f of subdivision 1 of section 239 of the
VTL to define a notice of violation.

Section 9. Amends paragraph f of subdivision 1 of section 239 of the
vehicle and traffic law regarding notices of violation.

Section 10. Amends subdivisions 1 and 1-a and paragraphs a and g of
subdivision 2 of section 240 of the VTL regarding technical changes to
notices of hearing.

Section 11. Amends subdivisions 1 and 1-a and paragraphs a and g of
subdivision 2 of section 240 of the VTL regarding formal notices of
hearings, contesting of fines, and records of bearings.

Section 12. Amends subdivisions 1 and 2 of section 241 of the VTL
regarding hearing officers, and hearings.  Section 13. Subdivisions 1
and 2 of section 241 of the VTL is amended regarding contestation of
liability.

Section 14. Paragraph a of subdivision 5-a of section 401 of the VTL
makes technical.  amendments to the VTL.

Section 15. Paragraph a of subdivision 5-a of section 401 of the
vehicle and traffic law is amended to prohibit the registration or
renewal of a motor vehicle if an applicant has three or more

outstanding red light camera violations under the foregoing
provisions.

Section 16. Amends the VTL to add a new section 1111(b) to authorize
the city of Syracuse to adopt a local law establishing a red light
camera demonstration program at fifty intersections throughout the
city and imposing monetary fines for violations thereof. The section
further outlines the parameters for establishment of such program as
well as penalty provisions.

Section 17. The opening paragraph and paragraph (c) of subdivision 1
of section 1809 of the VTL is amended to make technical changes.

Section 18. Subdivision 1 of section 1809 of the VTL is amended to
make technical changes.

Section 19. Paragraph a of subdivision 1 of section 1809-e of the VTL
is amended to make technical changes.

Section 20. Subdivision 2 of section 87 of the public officer's law is
amended by adding a new paragraph k to include photographs,
microphotographs, videotape or other recorded images prepared under
authority of section 1111 (b) of the VTL.

Section 21. Makes the purchase or lease of equipment for establishment
of red light camera programs subject to section 103 of the general
municipal law.

Section 22. Establishes the effective date and sunset of such program.

 EXISTING LAW :
New York city is currently the only municipality authorized to have a
demonstration program utilizing red light cameras.

 JUSTIFICATION :
In 1988 the New York State legislature enacted legislation that
allowed New York city to establish a demonstration program to install
photo monitoring devices to record vehicles going through red light
signals at traffic intersections. "Red Light Camera Programs" have
proven to be an effective traffic safety measure that prevent injuries
and the loss of life due to accidents caused by red light running.

Since its inception in December of 1993, hundreds of thousands of
vehicles, including buses and taxicabs, have been caught going through
red lights by the traffic control monitoring devices in New York city.
In calendar year 2005 alone, 306,117 violations or Notices of
Liability ("NOLs") were issued to violators. A large number of traffic
accidents resulting in bodily injury and death to motorists,
passengers, pedestrians and bicyclists are due to the failure of
motorists to obey traffic control signals located at intersections.
"Right angle" and pedestrian accidents attributed to red light running
are among the leading causes of traffic fatalities. By reducing the
number of vehicles running red lights, the likelihood of "right angle"
and pedestrian type accidents is reduced. The extended use of these
devices has been shown to dramatically reduce the number of violations
at the intersections being monitored.

Red Light Camera Programs have proven to be an effective traffic
safety initiative whose success has been recognized by the State
Legislature and the New York City Council in their repeated
authorizations to extend the initial demonstration program. This
legislation would authorize the city of Syracuse to establish such a
demonstration program to further promote safety and decrease motor
vehicle accidents.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
None.

 LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
This bill will increase revenue for the city of Syracuse through the
placement of red light cameras at intersections throughout the city
should a local law be adopted to establish such a program.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the thirtieth day after it shall have
become a law and shall expire on December 1, 2014.

BILL NUMBER:  S3812A   REVISED 05/19/09

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, the general municipal law
and the public officers law, in relation to owner liability for
failure of operator to comply with traffic control indications; and
providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof


 PURPOSE :
This bill authorizes the city of Syracuse to adopt a local law that
would allow for the installation of traffic control photo violation
monitoring systems ("Red Light Cameras") at up to twenty-five
intersections throughout the city and provide for violations not to
exceed fifty dollars thereof.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
The bill authorizes the City of Syracuse to adopt a local law or
ordinance establishing a 5 year demonstration program to impose
monetary liability on the owners of motor vehicles for an operator's
failure to comply with traffic-control indications within Syracuse.
The bill authorizes Syracuse to install and operate traffic control
signal photo violation-monitoring devices at no more than twenty-five
intersections within such City at anyone time.

The bill provides for the form of the evidence of liability and its
availability for inspection in adjudicatory proceedings, requirements
for the information to be contained in notices of liability ("NOLs")
and the method for delivery to owners alleged to be liable.
Requirements relating to the adjudication process are provided. The
local law enacting such a demonstration program could provide for
penalties of no more than fifty dollars for a violation and no more
than twenty-five dollars for failure to respond. Additionally, the
Department of Motor Vehicles is directed to deny an application for
the issuance or renewal of motor vehicle registrations if the
applicant has three or more NOLs and/or parking violations within an
eighteen month period for which the applicant failed to appear or
failed to comply with rules and regulations following entry of a final
decision. The bill also contains provisions addressing owner liability
with leased or rented motor vehicles.

Additionally, the bill requires the demonstration program to utilize
necessary technologies to ensure that photographs produced by photo
violation-monitoring systems not include images identifying a
vehicle's driver, passengers or contents, to the extent practicable.
Recorded images would not be subject to FOIL. NOLs are not deemed a
conviction as an operator, therefore there would be no points on the
owner's driver license as it would not made part of the driver's
license operating record, nor used for motor vehicle insurance
purposes. The bill provides defenses to an allegation of liability:
there would be no liability if the vehicle was reported stolen and was
not recovered prior to the time the violation occurred, or if the
traffic control indications were malfunctioning at the time of the
alleged violation. Demonstration program equipment is subject to the
provisions of section 103 of the general municipal law. Finally, the
City is required to submit an annual report to the Governor and
Legislature on the results of the use of photo violation-monitoring
systems.

New York city is currently the only municipality authorized to have a
demonstration program utilizing red light cameras.

 JUSTIFICATION :

signals at traffic intersections. "Red Light Camera Programs" have

None.
